dimension_justifications.soundness: The byte-level accounting is genuinely correct: I re-derived every entry of Table 4 from the stated identity bytes(n,b)=ceil(n/64)(8b+4) at T=3807.25, and all six Table 1 Store values (136.235 / 34.683 / 9.661 / 9.395 / 7.536 / 56.438-consistent constants) and every printed ratio (3.93x, 14.10x, 14.50x, 18.08x, 2.41x, 8.46x, 5.84x, 3.7038x, 10.9965x, 11.3073x, 14.0969x, 3.590x printed vs 2.969x normalized, 2.5211x / 2.6496x / 4.1187x lower-cache sub-ratios, and the 3.5556x / 1.8824x / 6.4000x format ceilings) reproduce exactly. The 30.000 MiB FP32 excess, the 42.8% figure in Table 2, and the 60-MiB length-independent GDN constant are all mutually consistent. Eqs. 5-6 (conservative strided byte interval) are correct and the no-false-negative / possible-false-positive characterisation is right. Against that, three substantive gaps remain. (a) The method as specified in Section 4.3 is never executed: the implementation behind Tables 1 and 2 'materializes a full private copy of the dequantized entry per query, so it shares nothing and exercises neither borrowing nor copy-on-write', and every FORKAUDIT verdict comes from a full-prefix BF16 vLLM stack with no split depth and no quantization. No experiment in the paper runs the proposed dequantize-share-COW Read path. (b) The motivating memory model (Eq. 1) asserts that workspace 'is set by the request shape', but the paper's own Read inflates workspace by a per-request dequantized BF16 copy of the whole entry (28.683 MiB/request at this document length by Table 4) that is never measured, bounded, or discussed; by the paper's own numbers the total resident footprint crosses the 136.235 MiB full-prefix reference at roughly 4-5 concurrent requests per document. (c) Several reported numbers do not reconcile with each other (Table 2 dense TPOT vs Section 5.3; the tok/s column vs TTFT/TPOT; the 3.8% cohort-length reconciliation vs the paper's own component model, which requires 5.5%). Central capacity claim is supported; the ownership half of the paper and the deployment interpretation are not.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Definitions, equations and denominators are stated precisely and the appendix accounting (Appendix C) is exemplary and independently checkable. But the exposition materially obstructs evaluation. The abstract is a single dense block of hedged numbers drawn from three different executions and three different denominators, and a reader cannot tell without cross-referencing five tables which arm each figure belongs to. Adverse facts are placed where they are hardest to find: the audited fork's 1.950 vs 0.019 GiB generation-increment regression appears in one subordinate clause of Section 5.5 and in Table 18, and is absent from both the abstract and the contribution bullets, which report only the tie. Table 1 splits two executions into blocks with a shared header, Table 2 and Table 21 duplicate the same six rows, and Table 3's continued header carries a Delta-F1 column the archival block leaves empty. The Recall column is printed blank in every table. The reader must reconstruct the central caveat (that no experiment runs the proposed Read path) from statements scattered across the abstract, Fig. 1 caption, 4.3, 4.4, 5.1, 5.5 and 5.6.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The paper explicitly disclaims novelty of the quantizer (standard asymmetric affine, group-wise, as in FlexGen), of per-layer bit assignment (KVTuner, AsymKV), of split replay (CoMem), and of block sharing (PagedAttention). What remains is (i) a whole-entry storage denominator for a hybrid split-replay entry, which is a real but modest accounting contribution, (ii) one measured capacity-quality-latency operating point on one model, one GPU family, 60 items and two datasets, with strictly worse TTFT than both endpoints and no measured serving-capacity benefit, and (iii) FORKAUDIT, whose own Table 17 shows a persistent-base content invariant catches the motivating historical alias 8/8, so the increment is transition-time localization only, and whose ownership design (Table 18) yields identical allocator endpoints to the paper's own paged-prefix baseline while costing ~100x more generation increment. The '0 of 5 / 1 of 5' output-equality figures come from mutants selected to be semantics-completing. Useful, careful, narrow; significance to the ICLR community is uncertain.

paper_summary: Q-CoMem extends CoMem-style split-depth replay to a hybrid attention/Gated-Delta-Network backbone by group-quantizing the entire retained entry, not just the boundary residual: the depth-j residual plus the lower full-attention KV and the lower convolution/recurrent state a later query needs. An offline Write packs that entry with a standard asymmetric affine quantizer over 64-value groups with BF16 scale/bias; an online Read dequantizes it, is supposed to share only immutable document tensors and create request-local mutable state through copy-on-write and recurrent rebinding, then replays the query through the lower layers and reconstructs the suffix. A separate fail-closed trace protocol, FORKAUDIT, defines seven ownership/provenance targets with a coverage-plus-binding-plus-predicates pass rule. On 60 Qasper/2WikiMQA items with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on H20-3e, a frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy at j=7 reduces retained tensor payload from 136.235 to 9.661 MiB/document (14.10x; 10.9965x against an all-BF16 reference) at a paired F1 difference of -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99], while TTFT rises from 0.163 s to about 0.673 s and generated-token throughput falls from 13.38 to ~7.2 tok/s. FORKAUDIT passes seven targets over 96 configurations, but on a full-prefix BF16 vLLM stack with no split depth and no quantization.
strongest_verified_contribution: The per-component retained-state accounting is correct and independently checkable from the PDF alone. From the stated identity bytes(n,b)=ceil(n/64)(8b+4) and Table 4's component counts at T=3807.25 tokens, I reconstructed every Store value and every compression ratio in the paper exactly, including the two-denominator (native vs all-BF16) re-analysis, the disclosure that 30.000 MiB of the 136.235 MiB reference is FP32 GDN excess, and the explanation of why the printed split-to-frozen step of 3.590x exceeds the 3.5556x Q4 format ceiling while the dtype-normalised step of 2.969x does not. Reporting a whole-entry denominator for a hybrid split-replay entry, rather than the residual alone, is a real and correctly executed accounting contribution, and the honesty of separating packing from dtype narrowing is above the norm for this literature.
strengths: Every arithmetic claim I checked reproduces exactly: Table 4 component bytes, the group-quantization byte identity, all Store values, all compression ratios in Table 1, the 3.7038x/10.9965x/11.3073x/14.0969x all-BF16 re-analysis, the 2.5211x/2.6496x/4.1187x lower-cache sub-ratios, and the 3.5556x/1.8824x/6.4000x format ceilings. The 60-MiB length-independent GDN recurrent constant implied by Table 4 is consistent with both the 30.000 MiB excess in Table 1 and the 42.8% figure in Table 2's footnote.

The paper separates denominators unusually cleanly: retained tensor payload (Store), post-priming allocator delta, and unmeasured process/NVML memory are never mixed, and Section 5.6 states plainly that reducing Store does not prove lower peak VRAM or admitted capacity.

The reference-arm defect in the archival analysis is disclosed and repaired rather than hidden: Appendix B states that all 24 archival intervals used dense or split-Q16 as reference while the Store column used full-prefix, recomputes 18 intervals against full-prefix from the same 360 archived per-item F1 values, and reports that the previously published -0.39 understated the deployment-relevant loss by ~13%.

Adverse results are reported rather than suppressed in the body: TTFT is worse than both endpoints, throughput is roughly halved, the aggressive policy's interval is entirely below zero, the headline policy is stated to be selected on the same panel without multiplicity adjustment, and the interval is explicitly said not to establish equivalence or noninferiority.

Eqs. 5-6 give a correct conservative byte interval for affine-strided views, with the right soundness direction (no missed shared byte among represented rows, possible false positives), and Appendix E states the schema, phase obligations and adversarial tests concretely.
Table 7 (cohort-to-claim authorization) and Table 30 (artifact map) make the claim boundaries per cohort explicit, and blank cells are used for unmeasured metrics instead of zeros.
questions: What is the median (and mean) document length of the eight-item slice used in Table 2? Under the model implied by Table 4, Store_native(T) = 0.01953125*T + 61.875 MiB, so the printed 140.34 MiB requires T = 4017.4 tokens, i.e. 5.52% above the 60-item mean of 3807.25, and the frozen row's 10.01 MiB independently requires T = 4019.1 (5.56%). The stated 3.8% yields 139.06 and 9.899. Which number is wrong?

In Table 2 the no-cache dense arm has TPOT 648.75 ms, essentially equal to its 0.649 s TTFT. Does that arm re-run the full prefill at every decode step? If so, how is it a meaningful latency reference, and how is it reconciled with Section 5.3's statement that in the operating-point run 'TPOT stays between 54.4 and 56.0 ms at every arm' for the same nominal arm on a superset of the same items?

How are TTFT, TPOT and tok/s defined relative to one another in Table 2? Under tok/s = n/(TTFT + (n-1)*TPOT), the dense row is unattainable (its ceiling is 1.541 tok/s against a printed 1.36), the full-prefix row implies n = 5.3 generated tokens, and the Q8 and Q4/Q4/Q8 rows imply n = 7.3 despite reporting the same or nearly the same F1. What accounts for the difference?

What is the peak resident footprint of the per-request dequantized entry during Read? Table 4 implies about 28.683 MiB of BF16 working state per concurrent request at this document length, against 9.661 MiB retained. At what concurrency per document does Q-CoMem's total resident footprint exceed the 136.235 MiB full-prefix reference?

Along which axis are the 64-value quantization groups formed (channel, token, head, or flattened storage order)? Section 2 identifies the grouping axis as the distinguishing choice among KIVI, KVQuant and XQuant, but Section 4.2 says only 'groups of 64 values'.

What is the convention in Eq. 3 when a group is constant (u = m, hence s = 0)? And is the reconstruction x_hat = q*s + m performed with s and m already rounded to BF16, so that the stated packed sizes are exact?

Section 4.3 defines the fork as F_r(D) over K and G only. Where do the convolution state C_l and the boundary residual h_j^D sit in the ownership contract, given that Eq. 2 counts both and Appendix E's anchors include conv-family rows?

In Table 18 the borrowed-GDN arms cost 1.95 GiB of generation increment against 0.019 GiB for the materialized arms, at identical final and peak endpoints. Since 60 MiB of FP32 GDN state times 32 requests is 1.875 GiB, is the rebinding step simply deferring the same materialization to generation time? If so, what memory benefit does the borrow-and-rebind discipline provide over materializing at setup?

How does the 14.10x figure vary with document length? Because the GDN state is length-independent, the same Table 4 model gives about 16x at T = 1000 and about 11.9x asymptotically. Should the headline number be quoted with its length dependence?

issues.location: Section 4.3 (p. 4, 'the Transformers implementation behind Tables 1 and 2 instead materializes a full private copy of the dequantized entry per query'); Section 4.4 (p. 5); Section 5.1 'Executed systems' (p. 6); Section 5.5 (p. 8); Section 5.6 (p. 9); Figure 1 caption (p. 3)
issues.observed_evidence: No experiment in the paper executes the Read path the paper proposes. Tables 1 and 2 come from a Transformers implementation that, by the paper's own statement, 'shares nothing and exercises neither borrowing nor copy-on-write'; every FORKAUDIT verdict and the Table 18 allocator study come from a different system (vLLM 0.26 plus Transformers, full-prefix BF16 KV in 128-token pages, no split depth, no quantization, PG-19). The paper therefore has (i) capacity/quality/latency numbers for a copy-everything implementation of the packing scheme and (ii) ownership evidence for an unquantized, unsplit configuration, and nothing that measures the composed system described in Section 4.3. Section 5.6 concedes that 'ownership there transfers by design argument only' and that dequantized-view immutability, residual-chunk binding and packed-entry lifetime are untested.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's stated design is a dequantize-then-share-then-COW Read. Both halves of the evaluation deliberately avoid it. The composition is exactly where the risk lives: a dequantized view is a fresh tensor whose immutability, aliasing and lifetime obligations differ from those of a paged BF16 KV block, and the audit's seven targets were never instantiated on it. As it stands the contribution is two disjoint, individually bounded results presented as one system, and a reader cannot conclude that Q-CoMem as specified either works or is safe.
issues.required_fix: Implement the Section 4.3 Read (shared immutable dequantized document tensors, request-local mutable state, recurrent rebinding, tail COW) and (a) re-measure Table 1/Table 2 Store, TTFT, TPOT and F1 on that implementation, and (b) run the seven FORKAUDIT targets on the packed j=7 Q4/Q4/Q8 path, adding the three obligations the paper names as untested. If that is out of scope for this submission, retitle and rescope the paper as a storage-accounting study plus a separate ownership-trace protocol, and remove the composed-system framing from the abstract, Figure 1 and the contribution bullets.
issues.verification_test: Run the 96-configuration ownership factorial with the packed entry substituted for the full-prefix BF16 KV, at j=7 and Q4/Q4/Q8, and report per-target coverage and verdicts in the format of Tables 8-9; separately re-run the 60-item panel with the sharing Read and confirm the Store column is unchanged and F1 matches within the archived per-item values.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-target FORKAUDIT coverage/verdict table for the quantized Read path; a Table 1 replication produced by the sharing implementation.

issues.location: Section 3, Eq. 1 and the sentence 'workspace is set by the request shape, so the retained term is the only one that grows' (p. 4); Section 4.3 (p. 4); Section 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p. 6); Section 5.6 (p. 9); Table 4 (p. 17)
issues.observed_evidence: Eq. 1's argument is that M_active is method-independent, so S(D) is the only controllable term. But the implemented Read materializes a full private BF16 copy of the dequantized entry per query, which by Table 4 is 14.8721 + 2*3.7180 + 6*0.0625 + 6*1.0000 = 28.683 MiB per concurrent request at T = 3807.25. That term is method-dependent, scales with the entry, and is excluded from every denominator in the paper: Section 5.1 and 5.6 list 'active workspace' among the exclusions and it is never measured. Combining the paper's own numbers, resident bytes for one hot document under Q-CoMem are 9.661 + 28.683*N MiB, which exceeds the 136.235 MiB full-prefix reference at roughly N = 4.4 concurrent requests on that document; the full-prefix arm carries no comparable per-request duplicate because its state is shared paged KV.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper is explicitly capacity-first and its entire motivation rests on Eq. 1. If the design converts retained bytes into per-request transient bytes at a ~3x exchange rate, the capacity claim holds only in the single-concurrent-query regime, which is not the regime the introduction motivates (agents, tree search, best-of-N, multiple hot documents). Excluding the term while asserting that the excluded term cannot vary with the method is a defect in the accounting model, not merely an unmeasured metric.
issues.required_fix: Measure and report M_active for the Read path as a function of concurrency (at minimum N = 1, 8, 32 on one document), state the crossover concurrency at which Q-CoMem's total resident footprint meets the full-prefix reference, and correct the Section 3 sentence so it no longer claims workspace is method-independent. If the sharing Read of TS-01 removes the duplicate, report the residual dequantized-view cost instead.
issues.verification_test: Instrument the Transformers Read with the same byte-range-union estimand used for Store, capture peak transient bytes over the Read window at N = 1, 8, 32, and plot retained + transient against the full-prefix reference; check the reported crossover against the 9.661 + 28.683*N prediction from Table 4.
issues.evidence_needed: A concurrency-resolved workspace measurement under the same estimand as Store, and a corrected statement of Eq. 1's assumptions.

issues.location: Abstract (p. 1, 'lowers the post-priming allocator delta from 4.901 to 2.229 GiB final (54.5%) ... which our audited fork ties on both endpoints'); contribution bullet 3 (p. 2); Section 5.5 'Allocator endpoints under a controlled ownership factor' (p. 9); Table 18 (p. 27)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 18 shows four arms. The 4.901 -> 2.229 GiB final and 4.920 -> 2.843 GiB peak reduction is Full-copy KV/Materialized GDN -> Shared-doc KV/Materialized GDN, and that second row is labelled in the paper's own table as the 'Paged-prefix baseline'. The paper's contribution, the 'Audited hybrid fork' (Shared-doc KV/Borrowed GDN), reads 2.229/2.843, i.e. exactly the baseline, and 1.950 GiB generation increment against the baseline's 0.019 GiB. The reference against which the 54.5%/42.2% is taken is described by the authors as not an optimized baseline ('no serving engine copies a shared prefix per request'). The 1.950 vs 0.019 GiB regression appears only in one clause of Section 5.5 and in Table 18; it is absent from the abstract and from the contribution bullet, both of which report only the tie. Table 18's rows 1 vs 2 show the same ~1.95 GiB penalty from borrowing GDN even under full-copy KV, and 60 MiB of FP32 GDN state times 32 requests is 1.875 GiB, so the rebinding appears to defer rather than avoid materialization.
issues.why_it_matters: A two-significant-figure percentage reduction quoted in the abstract against an arm the authors themselves call a strawman, whose entire content against the appropriate reference is 0.0%, is a reference-arm problem of the same kind Appendix B repairs for the F1 intervals. Worse, the one endpoint on which the proposed ownership design differs from the baseline is the one where it is ~100x worse, and 1.95 GiB of extra generation-time peak is roughly 200x the entire per-document retained saving the paper is selling. Omitting that from the abstract while keeping the favourable half of the same comparison is selective reporting of an adverse result.
issues.required_fix: State in the abstract and the contribution bullet that against the paper's own paged-prefix baseline the audited fork's allocator saving is zero on both endpoints and its generation increment is 1.950 vs 0.019 GiB, or drop the 54.5%/42.2% figures from the abstract entirely and report only the paged-prefix comparison. Add an explicit sentence on whether borrow-and-rebind can ever beat setup-time materialization in bytes, given Table 18 rows 1 vs 2.
issues.verification_test: Report the full four-arm Table 18 in the main text with a fifth column giving each arm's delta against the paged-prefix baseline rather than against the full-copy control; confirm the audited fork's deltas are 0.000/0.000/+1.931 GiB.
issues.evidence_needed: Abstract and introduction text revised to name the paged-prefix baseline as the reference for the allocator claim.

issues.location: Table 2 (p. 8), no-cache dense row: TTFT 0.649 s, TPOT 648.75 ms, 1.36 tok/s; Section 5.3 (p. 7, 'TPOT stays between 54.4 and 56.0 ms at every arm'); Table 21 (p. 29, same row repeated)
issues.observed_evidence: Two independent inconsistencies. (i) In Table 2 the dense arm's TPOT (648.75 ms) equals its TTFT (0.649 s) to three digits, which is the signature of re-running the full prefill at every decode step; yet Section 5.3 reports that in the operating-point run on a superset of the same items and the same stack, TPOT 'stays between 54.4 and 56.0 ms at every arm', a ~12x difference for the same nominal arm that the paper never mentions. Section 5.3's own phrase 'honest dense recomputation' suggests the authors are aware Table 2's dense arm is not. (ii) The three timing columns do not compose. Under tok/s = n/(TTFT + (n-1)*TPOT), the dense row's ceiling is 1/0.64875 = 1.541 tok/s for any n, so the printed 1.36 is unattainable; the full-prefix row implies n = 5.28 generated tokens; the Q8 and Q4/Q4/Q8 rows imply n = 7.32 and 7.36 although Q8 reports the same F1 (39.14) as full-prefix and therefore presumably near-identical outputs. Nowhere does the paper define these three metrics or state the median generated-token count.
issues.why_it_matters: Section 5.3 and the abstract's 'timing is adverse' conclusion rest entirely on these columns. If the dense baseline in Table 2 re-prefills per token, its TPOT and tok/s figures describe a broken configuration and should not be tabulated beside the others; and if the three columns cannot be reconciled under any standard definition, a reader cannot check the throughput conclusion at all. This is the one table in the paper whose numbers I could not reproduce internally.
issues.required_fix: Define TTFT, TPOT and tok/s explicitly (what is timed, what is excluded, whether dequantization is inside TTFT), report the median generated-token count per arm, and either fix or remove the Table 2 dense row. Add a sentence reconciling Table 2's dense TPOT with the operating-point run's 54.4-56.0 ms range or state that they are different decode configurations.
issues.verification_test: For each row of Table 2, publish n, TTFT, TPOT and total wall time and check tok/s = n/(TTFT + (n-1)*TPOT) to within the median-composition slack; re-run the eight-item dense arm with a standard prefill-once-then-decode configuration and confirm TPOT lands in the 54-56 ms band.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-arm generated-token counts and metric definitions; a corrected dense latency row.

issues.location: Section 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p. 6, 'a 60-item mean against a median over documents 3.8% longer - with 0.000 MiB left to the accounting'); Table 2 footnote (p. 8, 'a cohort with 3.8% shorter documents'); Table 4 (p. 17)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 4 implies Store_native(T) = 0.01953125*T + 61.875 MiB and Store_frozen(T) = 0.001647949*T + 3.38672 MiB, since the 30 GDN convolution and recurrent states are length-independent (this is the same fact the paper uses for its 30.000 MiB excess and Table 2's 42.8%). Table 2's 140.34 MiB then requires T = 4017.4 tokens and its 10.01 MiB requires T = 4019.1 tokens, i.e. 5.52% and 5.56% above the 60-item mean of 3807.25 - not the 3.8% stated twice. At exactly +3.8% the model gives 139.06 and 9.899 MiB, leaving 1.28 MiB and 0.11 MiB (31% and 32% of the two gaps) unexplained. Neither cohort's document-length statistic is printed anywhere in the PDF, and the claim that 'the two implementations agree to the byte at all five retained configurations' on the eight shared documents is not backed by any table.
issues.why_it_matters: This is the one reconciliation the paper offers between its two deployment tables, and it is presented as complete ('0.000 MiB left to the accounting'). In a paper whose principal contribution is exact byte accounting, a stated reconciliation that does not close under the paper's own component model is a direct hit on the central credibility claim - even if, as seems likely, only the percentage is mis-stated.
issues.required_fix: Print the mean and median document token counts for both the 60-item cohort and the eight-item slice, correct the 3.8% figure, and show the two-line reconciliation explicitly (Store(T_8median) from Table 4 equals 140.34 and 10.01). Add the per-document byte-agreement table that supports the 0.000 MiB claim, or weaken that claim.
issues.verification_test: Compute Store_native(T) and Store_frozen(T) from Table 4 at the eight-item median length and check they equal 140.34 and 10.01 MiB to two decimals; independently check that the same T reproduces 15.89, 9.74 and 8.41 for the Q8, per-layer and Q4 rows.
issues.evidence_needed: Cohort length statistics and the per-document Store agreement receipts.

issues.location: Section 4.2 and Eq. 3 (p. 4); Figure 2(c) (p. 5); Section 2 'KV and state quantization' (p. 3); Appendix C (p. 17)
issues.observed_evidence: The quantizer is specified only as 's = (u-m)/(2^b - 1), q = clip(round((x-m)/s), 0, 2^b - 1)' over 'groups of 64 values'. Three things needed to reproduce it are missing. (a) The grouping axis is never stated, although Section 2 identifies precisely the grouping axis as what distinguishes KIVI, KVQuant and XQuant; for a 2048-dim residual and 512-dim K/V per token, per-channel versus per-token versus flattened-storage grouping give materially different quality at Q4. (b) Eq. 3 is undefined for a constant group (u = m gives s = 0 and a division by zero) and no convention is stated. (c) The dequantizer is never written, and since s and m are stored in BF16 the reconstruction error depends on whether s and m are rounded to BF16 before or after q is computed; the paper only says 'BF16 scale/bias metadata'. The byte accounting is unaffected (I verified it), but the F1 numbers are not.
issues.why_it_matters: The quality column of Table 1 - the -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] headline - is a property of the specific packer, and the paper is not reproducible at the level of that column from the PDF. Appendix A already concedes that the layer-policy search and aggregation scripts are unarchived, so the text is the only available specification.
issues.required_fix: State the grouping axis and tensor layout for each of the three state types, the degenerate-group convention, the rounding mode, and the exact dequantization expression including where BF16 rounding of s and m occurs. Add one sentence on whether the same axis is used for the residual, the attention KV and the GDN states.
issues.verification_test: Re-derive the Q4 residual bytes and one item's reconstructed tensor from the stated axis and confirm both the 4.1828 MiB/document figure and a published per-item reconstruction error; ablate channel-wise versus token-wise grouping on the four-item calibration set and report the F1 sensitivity.
issues.evidence_needed: A complete packer specification, ideally with the quantizer module's public interface.

issues.location: Section 4.3, the definition of F_r(D) (p. 4); Eq. 2 (p. 4); Appendix E anchors (p. 19) and Table 6 (p. 19)
issues.observed_evidence: The fork is defined as F_r(D) = {K_l^D, K_l^r}_{l in A}, {G_l^D, G_l^r}_{l in G}. It omits the convolution state C_l and the boundary residual h_j^D, both of which Eq. 2 counts in the retained entry and both of which appear in the audit: Appendix E's six preregistered anchors include three 'conv'-family rows, and Appendix E's coordinate universe is '60 = 30 x 2 persistent layer/family coordinates (thirty GDN layers x recurrent and convolution families)'. The expression is also not a well-formed single object (two brace-groups separated by a comma).
issues.why_it_matters: The ownership contract is the formal core of Section 4.3 and the object FORKAUDIT is said to validate. If it does not name every mutable state family the entry contains, the reader cannot tell which obligations the seven targets are supposed to discharge, and the mismatch with the appendix's conv-family anchors suggests the main-text definition is simply incomplete.
issues.required_fix: Extend F_r(D) to include the convolution family and state explicitly where h_j^D sits (immutable document tensor, presumably read-only for all requests), and fix the set notation to a single well-formed object.
issues.verification_test: Check that every state family appearing in Appendix E's anchor list and in Eq. 2 appears in F_r(D), and that each has a stated setup/transition/final obligation in the Appendix E table.

issues.location: Section 4.4, the TCB sentence (p. 5); Appendix A (p. 15, 'Trusted components are hook placement, Python/Torch-dispatch and tensor/storage semantics, and honest process scheduling'); Section 5.5 (p. 8, 'the honest-process assumption'); Appendix I (p. 33)
issues.observed_evidence: The main-text TCB enumeration lists 'capture/replay, the mandatory-slot schema, slot-to-live-tensor binding, and framework storage semantics'. The appendices add at least two more trusted components that the main text omits: hook placement, and honest process scheduling / the same-process assumption (Table 6 further notes that 'zero selected-context overlaps' means only that the selected context never entered an allocator cell, 'not that the wrapper was absent or perturbation-free'). Eq. 4's pass predicate is correctly stated as trace-relative, and the exclusions that are listed are honest, so this is an omission rather than a misstatement.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's stronger claim is that a pass is fail-closed and establishes phase-indexed ownership evidence 'within the TCB of Section 4.4'. A reader who takes Section 4.4's list as the TCB will over-read the guarantee, because the honest-process and hook-placement assumptions are exactly the ones an adversarial or buggy runtime would violate.
issues.required_fix: Make the Section 4.4 TCB list identical to the union of the appendix lists (add hook placement, honest process scheduling / same-process capture, and paused-capture semantics), and cross-reference Table 6's caveat on allocator-cell separation.
issues.verification_test: Diff the TCB items named in Section 4.4, Appendix A, Section 5.6 and Appendix I and confirm the main-text list is a superset of all of them.

issues.location: Abstract (p. 1); Section 5.5 'Falsification beyond output equality' (p. 9); Table 11 (p. 24); Table 12 (p. 25); Table 17 (p. 27)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 17 shows the persistent-base content invariant failing 3/3 and 5/5 on the pre-fix lanes, i.e. it catches the motivating historical alias on all eight cells - the same cells FORKAUDIT catches. So FORKAUDIT's demonstrated increment over a one-line conventional invariant is transition-time owner/layer/family localization, which the paper does state. Separately, the '0 of 5 / 1 of 5' output-equality figures in Section 5.5 are computed over the five mutants that are semantics-completing by construction (M1, M2, M5, M6, M7 in Table 11), a set selected for the property being demonstrated. The abstract nonetheless leads with 'A fail-closed FORKAUDIT trace validates immutability, copy-on-write, recurrent rebinding, and call provenance because output equality alone can miss state aliasing'.
issues.why_it_matters: The ownership half of the paper is presented as one of three contributions, and it costs pages, a 96-configuration factorial and eight appendices. If its measured increment over an existing content invariant is localization only, and its design shows no allocator benefit (see TS-03), the contribution is much narrower than the abstract's framing conveys.
issues.required_fix: In the abstract, state the increment as localization over a persistent-base content invariant rather than as detection, and note that the 0/5 and 1/5 figures are over mutants selected to complete semantics. Consider reporting what FORKAUDIT costs (capture overhead on the H20 path) so a reader can weigh the localization benefit.
issues.verification_test: Report, for each of the nine primary mutants, whether a persistent-base content invariant alone would fire, so the marginal set is explicit rather than inferred from Table 17.
issues.evidence_needed: A side-by-side detector column in Table 11 for the conventional invariant.

issues.observed_evidence: All compression ratios are reported at a single document length (the 60-item mean T = 3807.25 tokens under a 4,096-token cap) and their length dependence is never stated, although Table 4 makes it computable: the GDN convolution and recurrent components are length-independent, so the native ratio is about 16x at T = 1000, 14.10x at T = 3807, and tends to 11.85x as T grows, while the all-BF16 ratio rises from 10.9965x toward the same 11.85x. The paper motivates long-context and multi-document settings but reports one truncated-4K point.
issues.why_it_matters: The headline 14.10x is presented as a property of the policy rather than of a (policy, length) pair, and it moves by roughly 35% over plausible document lengths in the direction that matters most for the long-context motivation.
issues.required_fix: Add one sentence and, ideally, a short curve giving Store versus document length for the reference and the frozen policy, and quote the headline ratio with its length.
issues.verification_test: Recompute the ratio from Table 4 at T = 1000, 2000, 4000 and 16000 and check it against measured Store on a length-varying slice.
issues.evidence_needed: A length sweep of Store, which requires no new model runs beyond re-accounting.

ethics_concerns: No ethics concerns. The paper uses public PG-19, Qasper and 2WikiMQA data, involves no human subjects, and includes an ethics statement that correctly scopes out safety, bias and privacy evaluation while noting the dual-use point that efficiency can increase deployment scale. Anonymity appears preserved: authorship is anonymous, prior CoMem work is cited in the third person, and the artifact map uses neutral aliases. The main text ends at page 9 with the ethics, LLM-use and reproducibility statements on page 10, so the ICLR 2026 page limit is met.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an automated LLM-based reviewer operating under a PDF-only access mode. The model read the submitted PDF with pdftotext and page-image inspection, read the supplied ICLR 2026 rubric, and independently recomputed the paper's byte accounting and every printed ratio with a short Python script in a scratch directory (Table 4 component bytes, the ceil(n/64)(8b+4) identity, all Table 1 Store values and compression ratios, the all-BF16 re-analysis, the lower-cache sub-ratios and format ceilings, the implied cohort document lengths behind Table 2, and the TTFT/TPOT/throughput consistency of Table 2). No repository, source, sibling directory, prior review or author note was consulted. All scores and issue severities are the model's own judgement under the supplied rubric.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A Table 1 replication produced by an implementation that actually performs the Section 4.3 Read (shared immutable dequantized document tensors, request-local mutable state, COW, recurrent rebinding), showing the same Store and F1 - this alone would close the paper's largest gap.

FORKAUDIT's seven targets executed on the packed j=7 Q4/Q4/Q8 path, with coverage and verdicts reported for the three obligations the paper currently names as untested (dequantized-view immutability, residual-chunk binding, packed-entry lifetime).

A concurrency-resolved measurement of the per-request dequantized working copy under the same byte-range-union estimand as Store, with the crossover concurrency at which total resident bytes meet the full-prefix reference stated explicitly.
An end-to-end capacity demonstration: how many hot documents fit at a fixed device budget under Q-CoMem versus exact caching, measured rather than argued from S(D) alone.

A corrected and internally consistent latency table with defined metrics, per-arm generated-token counts, and a dense arm that decodes normally, plus reconciliation with the operating-point run's 54.4-56.0 ms TPOT band.

Store-versus-document-length curves and at least one second backbone (Falcon-H1 appears already available in the audit cohorts) to show the whole-entry packing result is not specific to one Qwen3.5 geometry at 4K.

A complete packer specification (grouping axis, degenerate-group convention, dequantizer including BF16 rounding of s and m) and release of the aggregation, bootstrap and layer-policy-search scripts that Appendix A currently lists as unarchived.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: If the 3.8% cohort-length reconciliation turns out not to be a mis-stated percentage but a real gap in the byte accounting, so that Table 2's 140.34 MiB cannot be reproduced from Table 4 at the actual eight-item median length.

If Table 2's dense arm is confirmed to re-prefill every decode step and the paper continues to present its TPOT and tok/s beside the other arms without flagging it, since the latency section's comparisons then rest on a mis-specified baseline.

If the per-request dequantized copy turns out to make Q-CoMem's total resident footprint worse than exact caching at the concurrency levels the introduction motivates, which would invalidate the capacity-first framing rather than merely bound it.

If running FORKAUDIT on the quantized Read path reveals ownership violations that the full-prefix BF16 configuration cannot exhibit, confirming that the audit and the method were kept apart for a reason.

If the frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 point's -0.45 F1 result does not hold on any second dataset, model or document-length regime, given that the operating point was selected on the same 60-item panel without multiplicity adjustment.
review_limitations: PDF-only access: I could not inspect the quantizer implementation, the archived shards, the bootstrap scripts, or any artifact named in Appendix J, so all reproducibility judgements are about what the PDF specifies, not about what the (unseen) package contains.

The eight-item cohort document lengths are not printed, so my derivation that Table 2 implies +5.5% rather than +3.8% rests on Table 4's component model being exactly the model behind Table 2; the paper states the two implementations agree to the byte, which is what makes that inference available.

My throughput-consistency check assumes tok/s = n/(TTFT + (n-1)*TPOT); the paper does not define the metrics, so some of the discrepancy could be definitional rather than erroneous - except for the dense row, which is unattainable under any n.
I did not attempt to assess novelty against the full quantization or hybrid-caching literature; that is another reviewer's lens, and the paper itself disclaims mechanism novelty.
